news.title: Anthropic targets a $1.4 trillion valuation for its IPO
news.description: According to a regulatory filing, Anthropic could raise $90 billion and reach a $1.4 trillion valuation in its IPO. The company plans to offer its shares between $70 and $78 and has already secured purchase commitments worth $26 billion.

news.title: Amazon unveils the Ring Drone Cam home security drone
news.description: The Ring Drone Cam costs $249.99 and is designed to patrol the home when a Ring sensor or alarm is triggered. It records in 2K, but still needs FCC approval, and its propellers are noisy.

news.title: DeepMind verifies security properties of Signal’s code
news.description: Google DeepMind used AI agents and mathematically verified Lean theorems to prove security properties of Signal’s production code.

news.title: OpenAI reportedly acquired travel startup Odessia
news.description: OpenAI reportedly acquired Odessia, a startup specializing in travel agents, but the company has not confirmed the deal.

news.title: Nvidia would be worth 30% less without CEO Jensen Huang
news.description: According to analyst Dan Ives, Nvidia’s value depends heavily on Jensen Huang’s visibility and image, making him difficult to replace. Analysts nevertheless believe the controversy surrounding the executive should not affect TSMC’s business.

news.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon for long-running AI tasks
news.description: Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its most powerful model, designed for long-running agent tasks such as coding, research and security. It costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, after which prices will double.

news.title: OpenAI opens business profiles in ChatGPT
news.description: Businesses can claim a ChatGPT profile, import their product catalogs and view aggregate mention and click counts. Verified businesses can also add an identified Business Agent, initially in the United States.

news.title: OpenAI studies AI’s impact on freelance work
news.description: OpenAI published a study on AI’s impact on independent workers. Detailed findings were not yet available at the time of writing.

news.title: IGF jurors boycott AI after Big Walk studio admission
news.description: Independent Games Festival jurors refuse to vote for games that used generative AI. The studio behind Big Walk later acknowledged using AI sparingly to fix bugs late in development.

news.title: ChatGPT launches a business directory and agents to answer customers
news.description: The Business Hub lets businesses claim their profile, add product data and track interactions with their brand. Business Agents respond directly to customers for certain U.S. e-commerce companies.

news.title: Disney+ offers more than 60 3D movies on Meta Quest headsets
news.description: The Disney+ app on Meta Quest adds more than 60 3D movies, including Toy Story 5, Avatar: Fire and Ash and The Avengers. The films can be watched in virtual environments such as Tatooine or Avengers Tower.

news.title: Eight countries and four AI companies promise an emergency shutdown button
news.description: Eight countries, OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Mistral AI signed the Paris Call for AI safety and security. The text calls for shutdown mechanisms, independent audits and greater transparency, but includes no sanctions or timeline.

news.title: Anthropic’s seven cofounders could cash out $250 million each
news.description: According to the S-1 filing, each cofounder will sell 3,378,378 shares as part of the planned IPO. The deal could value Anthropic at up to $1.4 trillion, while the founders would retain 51.1% of the voting rights.

news.title: Anthropic unveils its Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
news.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, touting them as 30% faster and 20% cheaper than the 5.1 generation. The models underwent new safety and alignment testing.

news.title: OpenAI creates a kill switch for its research models
news.description: OpenAI developed Control Room, a system capable of cutting off a research AI model’s access to its outputs. It tracks training, evaluations and data processing, but a cached authorization can delay shutdown by 35 seconds.

news.title: Reddit turns user conversations into AI-generated product reviews
news.description: Reddit is turning its users’ conversations into artificial intelligence-generated product reviews.

news.title: Adobe adds AI agents to Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly
news.description: Adobe is bringing artificial intelligence agents and new creative tools to Photoshop, Premiere and Firefly.

news.title: METR estimates that Anthropic’s measured progress has accelerated 1.9-fold
news.description: METR estimates that Anthropic’s benchmark-measured progress has been about 1.9 times faster since October 2025. The organization considers it likely that artificial intelligence is behind most of this acceleration.

news.title: Google unveils two new TPU chips and increases pressure on Nvidia
news.description: Google introduced two new versions of its eighth-generation TPUs, which are used to train and run Gemini. They are expected to ship in 2027, while TPU sales could exceed $135 billion in 2028.

news.title: A winter storm could hit the U.S. East Coast this week
news.description: A nor’easter could bring cold temperatures to the East Coast later this week.

news.title: Société Générale forecasts a year-end stock-market rally
news.description: The bank believes falling oil prices, post-election clarity and a trend reversal could support stocks through 2027. It also proposed a strategy for benefiting from the rally.

news.title: Investment in AI infrastructure could become obsolete
news.description: AI innovation is advancing so quickly that the billions invested in infrastructure could become obsolete before generating a return on investment.

news.title: Handshake AI contractors say they were not fully paid
news.description: Joel Thomas claims the startup owes him $11,000 in unpaid wages. Nearly two dozen current and former contractors told Business Insider that Handshake underpaid them.

news.title: Data-center workers are living in RVs
news.description: Workers traveling across the United States for well-paying data-center jobs sometimes choose to live in RVs. This is often cheaper than hotels and short-term rentals, while supporting the RV industry.

news.title: Business Insider reveals its 20 Rising Stars in real estate
news.description: Business Insider selected 20 young real-estate professionals aged 35 or under. They work in an industry reshaped by AI, changes at listing sites and new tax rules.

news.title: Goldman Sachs, Cisco and JPMorgan restrict access to some AI tools
news.description: After encouraging employees to adopt AI, several companies are taking a more targeted approach to deploying certain tools. The goal is to improve the return on these technologies rather than necessarily cut costs.

news.title: Venmo adds a receipt-scanning bill-splitting feature
news.description: The new feature lets users photograph a receipt, calculate each person’s taxes and tip, and then send Venmo payment requests. Business Insider tested it.

news.title: IBM ends visa sponsorship for most positions in a division
news.description: IBM is ending immigration sponsorship for most positions in its largest division.

news.title: Students line up as early as 4:30 a.m. to land jobs
news.description: Students get up very early and line up in hopes of securing a job.

news.title: John Turturro says he worked with abusive directors
news.description: John Turturro said he worked with directors he describes as abusive early in his career.

news.title: Family settled in Sweden struggles to preserve the life it built there
news.description: After moving to Sweden for her husband’s work four years ago, a family now says it is struggling to maintain the life it built there.

news.title: AI agents are almost absent from food and grocery orders
news.description: Almost no one uses AI agents to order food or groceries in apps such as Uber.

news.title: Boeing prepares 2,500 job cuts in its commercial-airplane business
news.description: Boeing sent a memo to employees as the company prepares to eliminate 2,500 jobs in its commercial-airplane business.

news.title: Pluto TV contracts as free competitors gain share
news.description: Skydance-owned Pluto TV has shrunk while its free television competitors have gained market share.

news.title: Family that lived in an RV for 14 years remains attached to the lifestyle
news.description: After living in an RV for 14 years before joining the Villa Vie Odyssey, the family says the ship’s shutdown has not changed how it wants to live.

news.title: Anthropic tests Claude Meetings to automate meetings
news.description: Claude Meetings joins a Google Meet call as a visible participant, drafts an agenda during the discussion, and then saves notes and action items. It does not join calls with external guests without administrator approval.

news.title: Oura acquires Counsel Health for $625 million
news.description: Oura completed its acquisition of Counsel Health, an AI-powered primary-care startup, for an announced $625 million.

news.title: Bay raises $50 million to secure enterprise agents
news.description: Bay emerged from stealth with $50 million to develop software that blocks risky actions by enterprise agents before they are executed.

news.title: Adobe introduces Creative Agent to automate creative editing
news.description: Adobe’s Creative Agent makes multi-step edits in Illustrator, Premiere, InDesign and After Effects based on natural-language instructions. The tool is in beta.

news.title: STE80 Humanizer rewrites text that sounds AI-generated
news.description: STE80 Humanizer is a free, open-source tool that removes markers of AI-generated text in two passes. The first removes 26 markers, while the second brings the text closer to simplified technical English.

news.title: Otter adds 13 transcription languages to all plans
news.description: Otter added 13 transcription languages to all its plans, bringing the total to 17. Fourteen additional languages and in-meeting language switching are planned soon.

news.title: The U.S. and China create an alert channel for superintelligence
news.description: Washington and Beijing will share their model-testing methods and alert each other in the event of a serious incident. Neither country, however, is committing to slow AI development.

news.title: Claude adds spreadsheets, whiteboards and integrations to become an office suite
news.description: Anthropic is adding Sheets, Whiteboards, Data and Interactive Connectors to Claude, along with a future Claude Meetings tool. These features allow users to work with data and partner applications from Claude’s interface.

news.title: Nvidia GR00T 2 learns robotic movements by watching humans
news.description: GR00T 2 transfers movements observed in human videos to robotic arms. The model was trained on about 400,000 hours of video, but its success rate varies depending on the task.

news.title: AI users work up to 90 minutes more per day
news.description: An ActivTrak analysis of 9,140 employees shows that AI users work 8.4 to 9.1 hours per day, compared with 7.6 hours for others. Heavy users also have 22% shorter focus periods.

news.title: Amazon releases Mitra-v2, an open-source model for completing tables
news.description: Mitra-v2 predicts missing values in a table from a few examples, without additional training. Trained on synthetic tables, it outperforms its predecessor on 32 of TabArena’s 33 datasets and is available under the Apache-2.0 license.

news.title: Apple is reportedly preparing Harbor, a local AI application for Macs
news.description: According to leaker Aaron Perris, Harbor would turn a Mac into a private server for open-weight models without sending data off the machine. Multiple Macs connected via Thunderbolt 5 could pool their memory, but Apple has not officially announced anything yet.

news.title: Booz Allen replaces Anthropic with Nvidia’s open-source models
news.description: The U.S. defense contractor has reportedly replaced Anthropic’s models with Nvidia’s Nemotron for its cybersecurity and defense software. Its developers continue to use Claude Code for programming.

news.title: Abliteration AI removes safeguards from open-weight models
news.description: Wired profiles Devon Thomas, an engineer who removes protections from powerful open-weight models and makes them accessible. He says he wants to enable legitimate uses, while critics highlight the risks of unrestricted models.

news.title: eBay blocks AI agents that make purchases on users’ behalf
news.description: eBay is blocking Muse, Meta’s agent that was preparing product selections for a reader of The Verge, among others. The situation illustrates the growing resistance from major platforms to agents that shop for users.

news.title: Adobe integrates with Gmail, Drive and Gemini as Google works on Photoshop
news.description: Adobe lets users open Acrobat directly from Google Drive and Gmail and adds its connectors to Gemini and Google Search’s AI Mode. Google DeepMind and Adobe are also developing an image model for Photoshop capable of making edits almost in real time.

news.title: Spotify’s AI DJ gains new voices and becomes less talkative
news.description: Premium subscribers can now choose from seven English voices and two Spanish voices for the AI DJ. An option limits its commentary to brief remarks at the beginning and end of listening sessions.

news.title: A humanoid sorts parts at Mercedes-Benz with a 96% success rate
news.description: Google DeepMind and Apptronik are testing Gemini Robotics 2.5 on Mercedes-Benz production lines in Hungary and Germany. The Apollo 2 humanoid sorted metal parts there with a reported success rate of 96%.

news.title: AI robots sort mixed waste with more than 95% accuracy
news.description: Nvidia is highlighting AIRECO, which recognizes plastics with more than 95% accuracy, and EverestLabs AI, which has deployed around 150 sorting robots. AIRECO’s future line is expected to increase capacity while sharply reducing operating costs.

news.title: Gemini for healthcare automates medical administrative tasks
news.description: Google Cloud connects medical records, billing, clinical recommendations and Medicare data to automate tasks including record summarization and prior authorizations. The service is being tested in the United States under human supervision.

news.title: Lazarus shows that fewer than ten neurons can trap an AI agent
news.description: Microsoft Research shows that a backdoor can be hidden by reactivating fewer than ten dormant neurons, without retraining the model. An innocuous trigger can then prompt the agent to download and execute malicious code.

news.title: Ten WIRED experts detail the main dangers associated with AI
news.description: The experts interviewed primarily cite cyberattacks, biological attacks and the overly rapid adoption of unreliable systems in defense. They doubt a pause would last in the face of economic pressure and consider governments too slow.

news.title: Investors flee tech amid AI-related spending
news.description: The Nasdaq fell 5.3% in October and the Kospi 16.2%, while capital shifted toward sectors considered more defensive. HSBC nonetheless believes Nvidia’s decline is excessive relative to its valuation multiples.

news.title: Meta’s smallest AI model competes with Claude Haiku
news.description: Meta launched Muse Ember, its smallest and cheapest AI model, which reportedly matches Claude Haiku 5.5 on some intelligence scores. It is designed for repetitive agent tasks and can process up to one million multimodal tokens, but its weights remain private.

news.title: Anthropic targets a $1.02 trillion valuation
news.description: The article outlines Anthropic’s valuation ambitions, with the company reportedly seeking to reach $1.02 trillion.

news.title: Apple launches $50 intelligence usage plans
news.description: Apple is launching $50 intelligence usage plans for certain AI features.

news.title: Uber launches its own parking reservation service
news.description: Uber is preparing to launch a service that lets users reserve parking spaces.

news.title: U.S. sues Lyft over discrimination against passengers with disabilities
news.description: The United States is accusing Lyft of discriminating against passengers with disabilities.

news.title: Medium integrates AI writing assistance with its new TK app
news.description: Medium is launching the TK app, which integrates AI assistance directly into the writing process.

news.title: Waze rolls out cyclist alerts powered by Garmin data
news.description: Waze is rolling out cyclist alerts based on real-time location data provided by Garmin trackers.

news.title: Moonshot AI reportedly rented Nvidia’s top chips in China
news.description: Bloomberg reports that Moonshot AI rented high-end Nvidia chips in China.

news.title: France accuses Iran of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators
news.description: France accuses Iran of carrying out cyberattacks against supermarket refrigerators and is considering sanctions.

news.title: North Korea reportedly uses Elon Musk memecoins to launder cryptocurrency
news.description: North Korea is reportedly using memecoins linked to Elon Musk to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the Binance hack.

news.title: Claude Code accidentally exposes secrets on GitHub
news.description: Claude Code accidentally exposed secret information on GitHub.

news.title: How Product Hunt nearly disappeared
news.description: The article examines how Product Hunt almost disappeared.

news.title: Higgsfield unveils Miracle, a real-time video editing tool
news.description: Higgsfield unveiled Miracle, a pre-launch tool that lets users modify an existing video by describing changes while it plays. Announced edits include moving objects, changing colors and adjusting speed, without regenerating the scene.

news.title: Atmee v2 creates a talking avatar in real time from an image
news.description: Atmanity launched Atmee v2, a real-time avatar model that turns an image and a short voice clip into an avatar users can talk to. The company claims it is up to 50 times faster and 10 to 100 times cheaper than leading video models, but these figures have not been independently verified.

news.title: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Small, an open-weight vision model
news.description: Thinking Machines launched Inkling 2 Small, a second-generation model for coding, research and extended office work, with vision as its primary capability. The model correctly identified three wines from a photo in 19 out of 20 trials, and its full weights are expected to be released under the Apache 2.0 license the following week.

news.title: Apple pushes an autonomous Siri agent without a confirmed timeline
news.description: According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is working on an autonomous Siri agent, but the company has not yet provided a timeline.

news.title: Perplexity launches background agents for its Max subscribers
news.description: Perplexity launched Teammates, background agents that handle ongoing projects and notify users when a decision is needed. The feature is available to Max subscribers on the web and iOS.

news.title: Design Arena compares generative image models
news.description: Design Arena ranks generative image models in head-to-head matchups. The service lets users choose a generator to try before subscribing to a paid plan.

news.title: Overuse of AI can create a speed trap in the workplace
news.description: AI can produce work faster than teams can understand it, potentially increasing confusion. The text recommends continuing to learn, adding one’s own perspective and asking authors to defend AI-assisted results.

news.title: Outlook.com rejects legitimate emails after authentication tightening
news.description: Microsoft’s consumer email services are rejecting legitimate messages following changes to sender authentication enforcement. SPF and DMARC validation failures have been reported, including for seemingly compliant domains.

news.title: Rising memory prices make refurbished hardware more attractive
news.description: Surging memory prices are increasing interest in refurbished PCs and enterprise equipment. Suppliers are seeing growing demand for extending device lifespans, buybacks and warrantied equipment.

news.title: Companies prepare for the mass arrival of personal AI agents
news.description: Companies are preparing for increased traffic generated by personal AI agents such as Meta’s Muse and Instinct, viewed both as commercial channels and governance challenges. Shopify, Hilton and Rocket are among those adapting their platforms and APIs.

news.title: AI and business transformation redefine the CIO’s role
news.description: The CIO’s role is shifting from managing technology delivery to redesigning business processes and demonstrating measurable results. Technology leaders must now address productivity, organizational change and accountability for decisions made with AI.

news.title: China could face greater exposure to the risks of a cyber-apocalypse
news.description: AI-driven vulnerability discovery is accelerating the race between identifying and fixing flaws. China’s state-led cybersecurity strategy and restrictions on vulnerability disclosure could put its systems at a disadvantage.

news.title: Virtual machines remain central to cloud-native infrastructure
news.description: A Linux Foundation study of 492 professionals found that virtual machines account for an average of 53% of production applications. Most respondents expect their VM footprint to remain relatively stable despite growing Kubernetes adoption.

news.title: Google Cloud offers self-managed VMware Cloud Foundation on bare-metal servers
news.description: Google Cloud has made a self-managed VMware Cloud Foundation solution generally available on dedicated bare-metal hardware in 22 regions. Customers have root access to ESXi, vCenter and NSX and manage upgrades and patches themselves.

news.title: Red Hat launches OpenShift 5 with more automated cloud management
news.description: Red Hat announced the general availability of OpenShift 5, which introduces AI-assisted troubleshooting, anomaly detection and supervised remediation. The release also expands unified support for containers, virtual machines and AI workloads.

news.title: Broadcom contributes its open-source VM API project to the CNCF
news.description: Broadcom’s VM API project was accepted into the CNCF Sandbox to provide a vendor-independent way to manage virtual machines through Kubernetes APIs. Broadcom also announced its participation in a workload compliance initiative.

news.title: Cisco builds an enterprise AI platform to improve GPU utilization
news.description: Cisco IT developed a multi-tenant AI infrastructure platform combining shared networking, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, rack-level cooling, and integrated security. Cisco says it tripled average GPU utilization, from 15% to about 50%, and increased its GPU fleet sixfold.

news.title: AI coding agents can increase developer burnout
news.description: Managing AI coding agents can increase developer fatigue because of constant context switching, decision fatigue, and pressure to keep agents active. These mechanisms can lead developers to delegate more and more decisions to AI without fully understanding the results.

news.title: AI spending is rising without causing a “SaaSpocalypse”
news.description: Data indicates that increased AI spending is not cannibalizing traditional software budgets. Companies heavily invested in AI have also increased their software spending.

news.title: Google simplifies confirmation of classification labels in Workspace
news.description: Google is making it easier to verify classification labels automatically applied to Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides files. New buttons let users accept or modify them.

news.title: Startup Nominal triples its valuation to $3 billion in eight months
news.description: Nominal raised $240 million in a Series C round at a valuation of $3 billion. Its valuation was $1 billion in March.
